lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Experience is not in reverse chronological order; Crestway should come before Lakeview.
items.because: Greenleaf can remain first because it is the current role.

items.says: Replace any placeholder phone number, email, or profile URL before applying.
Make sure the profile supports the résumé’s dates and claims.
Add a service or reliability measure if available.
items.because: Delivery count alone shows workload, not performance.

items.says: Include the payment responsibility only if it matters to the target jobs.
Clarify the scale or operational importance of the wedding-order and cooler work.
items.because: As written, it describes duties without showing what the contribution improved.

items.says: Say what changed because of the pick-path layouts or labor reports.
items.because: “Owned” establishes responsibility, but the reader cannot assess the result.

items.says: Label the returns-time measure as total elapsed time or hands-on processing time.
items.because: The before-and-after figure does not say which it measures.

items.says: Ensure the trailer-wait comparison uses the same definition and measurement period.
Split or sharply narrow the cycle-counting bullet.
items.because: Unrelated supervision, training, hiring, and certification duties obscure the inventory result.

items.says: Clarify how much of the accuracy gain is attributable to cycle counting.
Verify that the stockout and inventory results cover comparable periods.
Verify that the forecast model materially contributed to both results.
Add the cost basis or period for the 15% freight reduction.
items.because: Readers need to know what it was measured against.

items.says: Clarify the outcome or decision enabled by the reorder points.
items.because: The data and method are specific, but the result is missing.

items.says: State what changed after buyers renegotiated delivery windows, if measured.
items.because: Otherwise, the claim should stop at the scorecard and its use.

items.says: The ending OEE figure of 112% is invalid.
Verify the starting and ending OEE figures against the underlying calculation.
The lead-time, throughput, and WIP figures appear internally inconsistent.
items.because: For the same process and period, halving lead time at constant throughput conflicts with doubling average WIP.

items.says: Clarify whether the 18% route-mile reduction is modeled or achieved.
Account for any operational constraints included in the routing comparison.
Clarify what drive times were compared and whether the comparison validates the proposed routes.
items.because: Predicted times for proposed routes cannot be directly validated against actual times on different historical routes without an appropriate comparison.

items.says: Add the pilot’s observed outcome if available.
items.because: Otherwise, the claim should end at the pilot rather than imply modeled savings were realized.

items.says: Narrow the operations-analysis bullet to the specific problem addressed.
items.because: It adds little beside the more concrete bullets.

items.says: State your role in mapping the intake process and removing steps directly.
Verify how the one-day improvement was measured.
The food-bank forecast appears to duplicate the Crestway achievement.
items.because: The product and warehouse counts, stockout improvement, and inventory reduction closely match.

items.says: If the forecast is separate work, distinguish the organizations, periods, contributions, and verified figures.
items.because: Its figures closely match the Crestway bullet.

items.says: Substantiate the level of Excel and Python skill implied by the project bullets.
